title: fail-safe output
invalidated_by: Any reviewed edit to these entries; bump version.
site_procedure_line: Anything that opens an enclosure or touches the circuit follows your site's lockout procedure with the equipment out of service.

rules.shared_cause: Several channels came in at the same time on this screen — look first for something they share (cable, connector, junction box, load supply) before chasing separate faults.
rules.consequence: The passivation messages are most likely the safety program's response to these wire breaks. This screen doesn't show which passivation belongs to which channel.

entries.means: The output channel reports that it cannot detect its load — the module's wire-break check tripped.
hypotheses: An open circuit between the output and its load: wire, terminal, connector, or the load's own coil or element.
The load is connected but draws less current than the channel needs to detect it, for example after an actuator or relay was replaced with a different type.
checks: Read the full time of each alarm, to the second, from the alarm history or the controller's diagnostic buffer, to see which came first.
Read the module and channel diagnostics on the HMI diagnostics page or online in the engineering software in view mode only — do not enter configuration or change any setting in the controller.
On the drawings, find what each listed channel drives and what those circuits share: cable, connector, junction box, load supply.

entries.means: The safety program switched this channel to its fail-safe value because of a fault it was told about: an output channel goes off, an input channel reads as its safe value. It stays there while the fault is present.
hypotheses: A channel or module fault the module reported to the safety program.
A communication fault between the controller and the module. The diagnostic buffer tells these apart.
checks: Read the full time of each alarm, to the second, from the alarm history or the controller's diagnostic buffer, to see which came first.
Read the module and channel diagnostics on the HMI diagnostics page or online in the engineering software in view mode only — do not enter configuration or change any setting in the controller.
On the drawings or a printout of the hardware configuration, find which module the F-I/O start address belongs to and what its channels drive or sense.
does_not_prove: which channel or module is at fault
